column8: Mon 16 Nov: 3c/3e: the moved half's plain three-year dollar loss chance on world data since 2001 (about one start in eight); script re-run, output identical; say month-end, dollars and one era (28 of 35 losing spans from one crisis).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e context only (the range is stated in dollars); 2001+ real shares re-run and match; the 1970-2000 calendar 18.5% rests on the unverified Wikipedia table; US CPI is not Taiwan building costs.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; NUMBERS 8r already tests the move date inside 2031, so the four-year case adds little; 2001+ figures re-run and match, 1970-2000 calendar figures UNVERIFIED.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b data behind row 38; figures re-run and match; quote NUMBERS 8f's 18.3% and 10.5% as the plan's and this row only as world history; the 1970-74 real figure rests on the unverified table.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 clash watch on IPS l.9; fix before use: borne out by history reads as shares are safe over six years, so add the survivorship caveat (row 20, the US was the survivor; ACO's 39 markets) beside the real 9.6%; its disanalogy cites row 23 for DMS 1916-20, which is row 28.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3/3e: the aha holds only on the unverified 1970-2000 table; on verified 2001+ month-ends real losses also fell with the wait (15.6% at three years to 9.6% at six), only more slowly than dollar losses (12.7% to 0%); say that, or verify the 1970s at MSCI first; US CPI is not Taiwan costs.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e illustration of row 6 (1970-74 -6.5% in dollars, -32.1% real); rests wholly on the unverified pre-2001 table; US prices, not Taiwan building costs.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3: joins IPS l.9 to why only the move-date value matters (8p); figures re-run and match; fix: the ending-in-a-loss share falling to 0% at six years must carry the real 9.6% and the one-era and survivor caveat, or it reads as shares are safe over six years.

Mon 16 Nov: Table 2 note and 3c: 8p's 40% test is worse than any month-end three-year dollar result since 2001 (worst -38.0%, Feb 2006 to Feb 2009); re-run and matches; pair with row 29 on counting conventions.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c process point (the move is a trade day, not a month-end); fix the source label: 57.46% is MSCI World's gross drawdown (World factsheet, store Q6c-004), not the ACWI factsheet (ACWI 58.38%); stays approximate, Mar 2006 interpolated (Oct 2007 level 5,164.82 checks).

Mon 16 Nov: Table 2's note: a plain yardstick for the named 40% stress; say about twice against month-end World (-19.7%), or two to two and a half times with the calendar -16.5% (pre-2001 era unverified); never against the house model, whose 1-in-20 is about -25%.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c and Table 2's note: names the two 40% events in one sentence; house 0.94% and US 1.1% are in NUMBERS 8p; adds 0 of 275 world month-ends; the distinction itself is store Q6c-013 and Q6c-021, so R 3; never rarer than 1 in 100 in prose (8p).
Mon 16 Nov: 3c: on the plan's own calendar (January buy, early-2031 move) 4 of 23 January starts lost since 2001, from two episodes; re-run and matches; say which count is meant.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b; figures re-run and match; fix: none of 20 at six years in dollars needs the survivor and one-era caveat beside its real count (2 of 20), or it reads as shares are safe over six years.

Mon 16 Nov: store only; the latest three years are the best only for MSCI World (+92.0%, Sep 2022 to Sep 2025); ACWI's best was +95.6% (Mar 2003 to Mar 2006), so name the index; context, never a forecast.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c, IPS l.15 in numbers; but stated-top frequencies on world history are plan figures not in NUMBERS (section 4 has US history only): the numbers owner adds a world column, or it is said strictly as a Keel arithmetic mapping; its since-1970 line rests on the unverified pre-2001 table; mapping re-run and matches.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e aha, but not the register's figures: the engine takes 17.88% as the log s.d. (engine.py eq_vol; 8p's 0.94% and 8f's 18.3% follow from it), giving about 24.2, 20.9, 18.3 and 16.1% at 3-6 years and a 1-in-20 three-year -25.4% (Keel arithmetic), not 22.1% and -21.9%; only 18.3% is in NUMBERS; the model is the pessimist on depth too.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e backing only (15.8% against 4.2%, 10.1% against 12.6%, read at source); 30-year real horizon, and the paper's lognormal is iid monthly, not independent years; never a 3-6 year claim about the house model.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 and 3f (the world fund's case); b=120 column read at source; fix the use: ACO's international portfolio excludes the home market and for a US investor lost more often (row 20), so state it as the typical developed-market investor's payoff, never as VT's measured payoff for Laura.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e: NUMBERS' US-history column is the survivor's record (1.2% against 7.6% at 30 years, read at source); extends store Q39-019 and H4-059 to 1-30 years; the survivorship caveat other rows need.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b; fix the plan figure: the house model's five-year loss chance in NUMBERS is 18.3% (8f), not the face-value 16.1%; nominal local currency, and which panel is home is Keel's inference.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3, against shares are safe if you wait; quote and Table VI figures checked at source; price only, so pair with row 23 (Jorion's total-return table gives the global index 30.2, 18.2 and 12.0% at 1, 5 and 10 years).

Mon 16 Nov: 3e presentation rule (say whether dividends are in); 12.0% against 19.9% checked at source; the Gaps' missing global total-return rows are in the same table: 30.2% and 18.2% at one and five years.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b; the VAR quote and -20.8, -40.4 and -41.1% checked at source; fix the use: the IPS keeps half unpromised as flexibility, not because of its horizon, so say only that its bad case is larger; the history twin of store H7-041.

Mon 16 Nov: store and 3e; -43.2% (Oct 1974) and -51.4% (Jun 1949) checked at source; fix the use: a fall before the move also lowers the top to about $105,000 (NUMBERS 8p), so only a fall after the move costs only flexibility.
Mon 16 Nov: 3e context: with dividends the worst case shrinks after five years, so the plan's 3-6 year horizons sit near the worst; annual DMS data; read with row 24.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; 20-30 year horizons are not Laura's share horizons; carries its survivor caveat (Japan, Germany, Belgium); Morningstar read from a copy on a third-party blog.
Mon 16 Nov: 3b: the world record's five-year real worst (-58%, 1916-20, 2024 Yearbook); name the vintage (row 35); real terms, not the dollar test the range uses.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3e presentation: name the count (calendar, month-end or trade day); DMS quote read at source; -43.5% is approximate and -41.5% rests on the unverified 2000 return.

Mon 16 Nov: 3c: why history counts are never probabilities for the promises; arithmetic checks (56 and about 26 years of data); agrees with SKELETON 3c's four independent rate eras for the 585 windows.
Mon 16 Nov: 3c and 3e: quote checked at source (Oct 2025 working paper); backs the split: the top rests on history and moves, the bottom rests on Treasuries and does not.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 and 3a: Siegel's real-return comparison does not apply to dollar promises held to their date (-11% a year is about -44% over five years, checks); edition with data to 1996 on a hosted copy, so S 4.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; the long-run US and world records carry their survivor caveat; Laura's share horizons are 3-6 years.
Mon 16 Nov: store only; beating bills is not the half kept's test; US real data to 1996.
Mon 16 Nov: references and 3e: quote one DMS vintage and name it, preferring the 2024 Yearbook; the conflict is recorded, not resolved.
Mon 16 Nov: references: cite MSCI World gross for long history; ACWI before launch is back-tested; the two launch dates stay unresolved.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e stand-in check (largest monthly gap 1.15 points, re-run); fix: the six-year worst +5.0% and +4.6% is dollars only (real -6.3% and -7.8%) and one era, so say so or drop it; VT's FTSE index not computed.

Mon 16 Nov: 3b: world history's five-year dollar loss (6.4-11.5%) sits near NUMBERS 8f's US 10.5% and under its house 18.3%, so 3b quotes the register's cautious figure; row 17's aha on register figures; the 11.5% rests on the unverified pre-2001 table.
